utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. No preliminaries. We wait for the witness to enter the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Maksimovic. Before we continue, I'd like to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you have given at the beginning of your testimony. Ms. Bibles will now continue her cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, on Friday you agreed to review a statement for us.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And I'd ask that 65 ter 30888 be brought to our screen. We can start on page 8 in English and 9 on B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, this was a lengthy statement that you were given before you left. Did you have an opportunity to review it this weekend?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did go through it. I read it from first to last page.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'm going to direct your attention to a few points picking up with where we left on Friday. You can see -- I see that you have the statement in front of you. You can also see it on the screen in front of you. We see at the bottom of page 8 in English and page 9 in B/C/S a discussion of the shooting of Ziko Krajisnik that we looked at on Friday.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could now turn to page 9 and the top of page 9 in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: We see at the very first line a soldier shouts: "People, what is this - we have our prisoners in Sarajevo." Were there Serbs being held prisoner in Sarajevo at this time?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you honestly, I could neither confirm nor deny since I was a soldier at the time who had been given a task to perform together with his unit. Perhaps there may have been or not. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: A few paragraphs later Mr. Koblar describes that he was next taken to Blazuj to the military police barracks. Do you know whether this was standard practice for prisoners?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I encountered prisoners for the first time at the time. Therefore, I don't know what standard practice was. I told you last time that when we captured those ABiH soldiers, my unit handed them over to the military police and we went about our next task. Perhaps it was practice to have POWs moved to the barracks. Perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And at -- you testified as well on Friday regarding taking three prisoners, ABiH prisoners. As we go down the page, we see that Brne mentions to officers at the military police barracks that prisoners had been killed, and the officer said: "Told Brne that they had three more prisoners from Golo Brdo including a Serb." Would it make sense that those were the prisoners that you had referred to in your testimony?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most possibly. I really don't know, as I said, because I went together with my unit towards the Obeljak and Stupnik hills to the right. Therefore, all of this that I could read in the statement is something I'm not familiar with. I can see that the statement was drafted very carefully with much detail and a lot of sound descriptions, but I can't tell you precisely whether they were the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Did you ever hear whether your prisoners, like Mr. Koblar, were eventually taken to Kula?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I learned that when I returned from the school. Something to the effect that Koblar had run away and that he was at Kula. I heard that from some people at Mrkovici when I assumed my duty as platoon commander [as interpreted] there. In one of the conversations I had I realised it was the same man we were talking about.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And with respect to that, just to clarify the order, you understood that he was taken to Kula and then he escaped from Kula?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that by the time I arrived at Mrkovici after my training. I took part in that operation and then I went to Banja Luka for further education and then I was transferred to the Mrkovici unit. Then I learned that he had been there and fled.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Page 3, line 17, it should be "company commander" instead of "platoon commander."

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Now you, having read the entire statement, if you go to the end, you would agree that we read that Mr. Koblar escapes from Kula in February 1994. Is that consistent with your recollection?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In terms of date and time, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Maksimovic, a few moments ago you testified that the statement is very detailed. Having read the entire statement now, I'll ask you again what I asked on Friday, and that is: Do you have any reason to dispute the account of the murder of Zika Krajisnik as it was provided in Mr. Koblar's statement?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no reason to dispute it or to say anything positive, so to speak, about this statement. It does strike me as strange that he could recall so much detail, describing the people, their height, weight, and looks, being constantly under stress and mistreated psychologically and physically. That is what was a bit unclear to me in all of it. My only conclusion is that he must have been in very good physical and mental state as he was drafting this and throughout his imprisonment. The person in question must be highly intelligent, I presume. The presumption is that when one is in difficult surroundings, that person cannot describe people, events, and movements in such a good way. I'm not trying to say that I doubt what he stated in his statement but that he is pretty --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you are drawing all kind of semi-psychological conclusions on the statement which was not the question. The question was whether you have any specific reason to doubt. But then I think that Ms. Bibles meant to say any knowledge you have which would shed a different light, rather than your psychological insight in the condition of someone who's in detention. Please proceed, Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: We'll shift -- we'll finish my questioning in a different direction now.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And I'd like to -- we'll go to an interview that you gave with "Javnost" at the end of this. But to -- just to make sure that -- that we're going down the right direction here, is it accurate to say that there was times with -- when you spoke with the media or with the public regarding your work with the VRS?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the war there was an interview taken at Spicasta Stijena. I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Is it accurate that you and others received guidance as to how to communicate with the media or with the public, and you received this from the Main Staff through the chain of command?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember whether there were some specific instructions, but I think I conducted myself in a soldierly way at the time. I can't recall precisely whether any instructions had been received.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Let's see if we can refresh your memory.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could see 65 ter 30892.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And, sir, this is a document containing guidance regarding public information. And, sir, now that the B/C/S version has come up, I'd ask you to look in the upper -- I believe it's the left-hand corner of this document. We see here a military post code for Igman Brigade listed as 7066. Was that the correct military postal code for the Igman Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: The first paragraph of this document describes that this is a VRS Main Staff document which is being passed on in its entirety. Is it true that before reaching the brigade level a document like this would have been disseminated versus the SRK Corps command?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I missed a part of the question. What -- is what true?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If this document had come from the Main Staff to the brigade level, would it also have gone to the SRK corps level first before it came to the brigade level?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And we could now turn to page 2 in the B/C/S -- actually, in both.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'll have you look at the stamp and the signature and see if you can tell us if this is the correct indicia of an authentic Igman Brigade document.

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you have in mind -- oh, yes. Yes. There is a signature, assistant commander for religious affairs and morale, as well as the stamp of the military post.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Would dissemination of instructions like this have been the responsibility of that officer?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Now, looking at the date of this, I recognise that it is the 20th of November of 1994, and I recognise that you were with the 1st Romanija Brigade on that date. Do you recall receiving a similar document?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember. Different documents arrived. Now, whether this one was among them is something I can't say. It probably was. If it came from the corps command and it went down to the brigade command, it was probably distributed further down to the commanders or battalions and companies.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Would you have followed this type of guidance when speaking with the public or with the media?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if it was an order, then of course. If it contained express orders by superiors, as company commander I would of course have to abide by it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender 65 ter 30892.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30892 receives number P6632, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could bring up 65 ter 30858 now.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: While this is coming up, I'll ask you whether in late 1994 when you went back to the Igman Brigade you were the company commander at Golo Brdo?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My initial appointment with the Igman Brigade upon my arrival from the 1st Romanija Brigade was commander of the sabotage and reconnaissance platoon and commander for recruit training. After that, perhaps a month or two later, I became commander of the company.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Were you in that position in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Now if we could leave the B/C/S version at this page and turn to page 4 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'll ask you, sir, in the B/C/S, to look at the third column towards the bottom right and see if you recognise your name. And, sir, this article refers to, in the initial stages, as the Muslim road of life. Do you know what that refers to?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's probably the road via Igman.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Do you know why it would be referred to as the road of life, the Muslim road of life?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because -- probably because it was the only route they could use to go in and out of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Maksimovic, I see that you had an opportunity to look at the screen here. You're quoted as saying: "Serbian fighters can block the road at any moment and cut off and completely close the Muslim Sarajevo in the basin." First, were you accurately quoted here? Are those your actual words?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Honestly, I don't remember it all. I don't even remember the interview very well. Let me just add, if I may, something about journalists and press agencies.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If --

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they over blow things out of -- always blow things out of proportion.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could just look at your statement itself. Although you may or may not recall the exact words that you used, would you agree that the statement as it was drafted here was completely true?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In my statement I conveyed what I remember about the period in the best possible way I knew how.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Maksimovic. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Bibles. Mr. Stojanovic, any questions in re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a few, Your Honours. While this document is still on the screen, I would like to pose a few questions about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Maksimovic, in the document - and you can have a look - we see your words purportedly. There one can read that you assert that Serb fighters can completely block the road at any time and completely cut off and close the Muslim Sarajevo in the basin. My question is: To the best of your recollection, was this a realistic assessment of the abilities of the VRS at the time?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Given the fact that we controlled that part of the road, I think it is. I think we would have been able to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: While occupying the duties you held, did you ever receive any kind of order from your superior command to cut off this so-called route of life to Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This road of life via Igman, did it have direct connection to the tunnel under the runway, direct access?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, but we didn't control that part of the route from my position. From there we could see about 1 kilometre of the road that we could cover by fire. Since all communication between Sarajevo and the rest of Bosnia-Herzegovina went along that route, it probably included the tunnel as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At the time did you have operational information or personal knowledge about whether Sarajevo was fully encircled by the VRS?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would have been had that route been cut off. If we had physically sealed it, it would have been the case. But that route was even used by the rapid intervention forces to bring in their weapons and the assets they placed in ABiH-controlled territory. In co-ordination with them, they attacked us. I saw that myself. It happened several days before the air strikes. They transported heavy assets and howitzers and placed them somewhere at Igman, and I personally experienced the bombing as well as the shelling, the bombing by NATO aircraft and the shelling by the howitzers themselves. Before that there had been an ABiH offensive. Its intensity did not come even close to the intensity of attack carried out by the rapid intervention forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have information that the Republika Srpska Army suffered casualties from rapid intervention forces?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two men in my unit were injured, my command post was hit, it was by chance that I survived. And in the morning at 4.00 or 5.00 a.m. when this happened I was alone at the command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You describe that in your statement, so let's not waste time on that. Just one question: Having regard of what was written in the article, you are quoted as saying: "We can see them running across the road. These are special groups. They wear bullet-proof vests, but not even double ones will help them." My question: How frequent were those groups passing across the road in front of your line that you held?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't specify because of the passage of time how frequent, but I do remember I could seem them several times. Probably special units traverse that area because not even in our army, not all soldiers carried the same kind of weapons. And from what we could see, they carried good equipment, bullet-proof vests, so they must have been some special units.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you at any time -- now being a trained officer, did you receive from your superiors -- did you receive any illegal order to act in an unlawful manner during those war operations?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Maksimovic, thank you very much for your assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic. Has the re-examination triggered any need for further questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. It did, however, remind me that I did not tender 30858 which I would do at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30858 receives number P6633, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6633 is admitted. Mr. Maksimovic, since the Bench has no further questions for you either, this means that we are at the end of your testimony. I'd like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and for having answered all the questions that were put to you both by the parties and by the Bench, and I wish you a safe return home again. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could take the opportunity. We had an issue with the translation on P6631. That has been revised and uploaded. We ask for permission for this revised version to replace the English translation currently in place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And any number available for Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I believe it's doc ID Y017-8927-1 ET.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles, could you please check if the number on the screen is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you. It should be "8927-1" as opposed to "81." Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, you have located the document?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may replace the old translation by the new version uploaded and just referred to by Ms. Bibles. If there is any issue with the new translation, Mr. Stojanovic, you have an opportunity to raise the matter within the next 48 hours. Is the Defence ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Pardon me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: There is one preliminary matter related to the next witness and I wonder if we might address it before the witness is brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We can do so. We can deal with it in open session?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, we can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Traldi, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Mr. President, this morning we received an updated exhibit list for the next witness, Mr. Rasevic, which included one video identified with 65 ter 1D02992. I'd just ask initially for an explanation as to the late notice as to the video and separately as to its omission from the Defence Rule 65 ter lists filed in April and May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whom to address? Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it is correct what my learned friend said. In discussions and proofing with the witness for his testimony, at one point I received information from the witness that he had occasion to see a video-clip on the internet showing ABiH [indiscernible] about an operation that they executed against the positions held by the witness's unit. Yesterday morning we searched the internet, we found that video-clip, and immediately notified the Prosecution thereof. And last night during another proofing session with the witness, he confirmed that this was that video and we decided to use two periods of one minute each concerning their attack on Spicasta Stijena.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Recently became aware of it apparently is the explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just to correct one matter that Mr. Stojanovic raised in his submission. What he said at lines 23 and 24 of temporary transcript page 13 suggest that we were notified of this video yesterday morning. Instead, we were only notified of it at 9.00 this morning, and we were only notified of the source of the video at or around 9.30 when the surrogate sheet was released in e-court. What that means in practice is we haven't been able to view the full video from which they have selected excerpts yet because, as came up last week in the context of Colonel Radojcic's testimony, we don't have YouTube access -- or at least most of us don't have YouTube access at the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, I heard Mr. Stojanovic -- Stojanovic saying: "Yesterday morning we searched the internet. We found that video clip," it doesn't say when he found it but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It does say immediately after that they immediately notified us so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- perhaps I simply want to make clear --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- it happened this morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- why was there no notification yesterday when you found the video?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I state, it's reflected in the transfer. Last night we met again with the witness to check with him whether that was the video that he referred to, and at 9.00 p.m. last night we finished that meeting, he confirmed, and then I probably because of technical reasons or because of inability to load it up on to the system the notification arrived only this morning. That's my prescription. If --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there was a fair chance if you located a video which you think is the video the witness talked about, then you should give immediately notice - perhaps not by saying, We are going to use this, but by saying, We found a video which we may want to use after verification with the witness. You should not have waited. That's the simple message. Mr. Traldi, I suggest that we just proceed and if you need further time, I don't know how long the video is, perhaps Mr. Stojanovic could tell us. How long is the video, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. Two excerpts from a video-clip which lasts slightly over 19 minutes. And those two excerpts are slightly longer than one minute each, so that would bring the total to two and a half minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And may I take it that you did not make these excerpts this morning so that yesterday you started working already finding excerpts. Another reason why you should have informed Mr. Traldi right away. Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just related to the video. We can tell from the description in e-court what location it purports to be of, and from Mr. Stojanovic's comments just now, we have information about how the Defence located it. There doesn't appear in the excerpts that we've been provided with to be any sort of chronological information as to what point in the war it was happening, and we haven't received a proofing note to that effect. So if the Defence intends to rely on it about any period, I'd appreciate if we'd be told at the very least at the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, are you able to tell Mr. Traldi when that video was -- is covering what period of time?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Last night we received information from the witness that to the best of his recollection - and this is what I'm going to ask him about - is that it was -- it concerned the summer of 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. We'll see. Mr. Traldi, you raised the matter. I do not hear any special relief you were asking for at this moment. Perhaps you'll reserve your right to ask for more time if viewing the video would necessitate you to ask for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That's right, Mr. President. I just may ask for specific relief later today depending on how the examination develops.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then is the Defence ready to call its next witness, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think so, Your Honours. By your leave, I would like to ask Mr. Usher to distribute summary witness statements before -- to the interpretation booths before the witness enters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, for the next time if you would give it already before court. We don't have to wait for the usher to rush around and deliver all the statements which he could have done before court, saving quite a bit of time. But we'll apparently wait. And at the same time consider this to be time used by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Before you give evidence the rules require that you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That you undertake the solemn declaration. The text is now handed out to you. I would like to invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You'll first be examined by Mr. Stojanovic. You'll find him to your left. Mr. Stojanovic is counsel for Mr. Mladic. Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: First, please give your information about your name and surname for the record.

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: My name is Blasko Rasevic, son of Jovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That would be enough. The next thing I would like to ask you about is did you at one point give a statement to the Defence of General Mladic in writing?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's please see document -- 65 ter document 1D01637. Let's take a look at page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rasevic, is the information on your date of birth, name of your father, et cetera, are they correct? And is this your signature?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this date is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now let's go to the last page of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is this your signature, Mr. Rasevic, on this document?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, Your Honours, let us focus now on paragraph 15 of this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Indiscernible] during proofing, did you inform us that there is a typing error in this name and that the name of the person that you referred to was not Vojo, with a V, but with a B, Bojo?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: That's correct. It slipped through my attention as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's take a look at paragraph 28 of this statement, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Here mention is made of the same person, mentioning Vojo, whereas his correct name is Bojo, with a B; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now let's go to paragraph 24 of that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Where you pointed out another typo for our benefit. You stated that the -- the boy referred to in paragraph 24 named as Jezic, whereas his real name is Jesic, with an S; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Now that we've gone through the corrections concerning those two spelling errors referring to persons that you mentioned, if asked the same questions now that you've given this solemn declaration in this courtroom, would you have given the same answers as stated here in your statement?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I would have given the same answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I move to tender into evidence this witness statement by Rasevic, Blasko, which is 1D1 -- 01637 as specified in the 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D1637 receives number D551, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D551 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Also, Your Honours, I propose that the corresponding exhibit be tendered into evidence showing -- it is a map showing the positions of his unit which is 65 ter 1D02098.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D2098 receives number D552, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D552 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your permission, Your Honours, I would like to read out the summary of Blasko Rasevic's statement. Witness Blasko Rasevic, until the outbreak of war incidents in Sarajevo, had worked as a bus driver at the GSP Sarajevo. At the end of 1991 and the beginning of 1992, on several occasions at different locations his bus was stopped, the bus that you use to move citizens about, and passengers, and he himself were asked to show ID documents by paramilitary units which carried different kinds of weapons, about whom he learned they were part of the Patriotic League and Green Berets. Seeing that interethnic relations were being more and more strained, he decided to take his family outside his home and went to his parents' house in the village of Mrkovici on the 4th of April, 1992. The inhabitants of the village self-organised to defend themselves and he became a platoon commander. Later on he became company commander, the Mrkovici Company commander, which duty he carries out until the August of 1994 when he was transferred to the Hresa Battalion command. He claims that his unit, while he was its commander, executed and received only defensive duties. He never received nor he issued an order to target civilians or civilian facilities. ABiH attacked the positions of his unit on several occasions. Sniping caused the most victims in his units, and such attacks constituted cease-fire violations. He could spot firing positions of ABiH from his positions which ABiH used to open mortar fire. Those positions were by the physical training school, then the Kosevsko Brdo tunnel, the Kosevo stadium, school-yard of Nemjan Vladkovic school, and inside the perimeter of the Kosevo Hospital. He also informed that enemy mortars were placed on trailers, vehicle trailers, to hide the firing positions. They would be placed behind schools, buildings, kindergarten, and hospitals. He personally saw on several occasions such vehicles coming from the direction of Sedrenik and going in the direction of his unit's positions. Your Honours, that would be the summary of this witness's statement. And maybe this would be the right time to break and after the break I would have several questions to ask of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How much time would you need for those questions, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Up to 10 minutes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Up to 10 minutes. Then we'll take the 10 minutes after the break. We'll take a break, Witness, a break of 20 minutes. We'd like to see you back after the break. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will resume at 10 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we are waiting for the witness to be brought in. Mr. Stojanovic, isn't it true that last week on Friday you provided a provisional suggested list to the Prosecution. We have seen that list, then in court later it was announced that you had reached an agreement with the Prosecution on how to proceed with what witnesses, and then Mr. Lukic asked -- here he announced that they worked hard on this issue and that he thought that had reached an agreement. And, he said: "Your Honours, would you like me just to send you a list or do you want me to ..." Then I said: "If you are in agreement, then the Chamber is -- it's unlikely that the Chamber would intervene in any way and then we would like to receive a list."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We never received that list. So next time if you announce lists to be sent, it would be appreciated if you do so, so that we -- and when I say "you" I'm addressing the Defence because it was Mr. Lukic who more or less promised it. Let's proceed. You said you would need another 10 mention. Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Can we please have the following document in e-court -- actually, I think it's before us. For the record, I wanted to say that it is D551.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rasevic, please focus on paragraph 22 of your statement as I will have a few questions. Therein in paragraph 22 -- 26, you say that your unit had no artillery. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "my unit," what do you have in mind specifically? Which unit?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: I had my company in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You go on to say that behind my unit's position some 2 or 3 kilometres away there was an artillery position with 122-millimetre mortars?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: My question is: Which unit did these mortars belong to?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: It was a mortar battery belonging to the Hresa Battalion, and they were commanded by the battalion commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you as company commander have the possibility to request support directly from the mortar unit?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not have that possibility. I could only go via my superior command. I couldn't insist upon it or request it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. During the proofing yesterday, did you at some point in time draw my attention to the fact that there was a video footage of attacks on your unit's positions?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there is footage. Anyone can see it on YouTube. I think it was in late July or early August when it happened, when the special units of the army of the so-called Bosnia-Herzegovina -- actually, the so-called Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and they were called Black Swans, attacked the so-called Spicasta Stijena, although we never referred to it as such. But we had three trenches there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, Your Honour, could we have a look at an excerpt?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: July of what year, Mr. Witness? You said, "July or early August." Of what year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Late July or beginning of August 1994. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Can we have a look at the excerpt from the footage on YouTube, starting with 5 minutes to 6 minutes and 14 seconds.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We have not received any transcript in case there is an audio recording.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any text we should look at, Mr. Stojanovic, or we should listen to?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. There is some text but we did not want to draw your attention to it because it is in the margins of what is going on and is not important for what we want to show. I think we should play it only once and that pertains to both excerpts we want to show.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We can do that. May I take it that you have provided the Prosecution with a version with audio included? Even if it's only in the margin.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We forwarded the two excerpts to them and we are preparing the text to the extent possible because not all of it is audible in the background.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You only forwarded two excerpts, not the whole of the video?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are preparing the entire footage. It is being re-recorded, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Re-recorded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, where are we? I mean, YouTube as a source and internet as a source is -- should be looked at in a very critical way. Did you receive, meanwhile, the whole of the excerpt or were you able to verify whether it's the entirety from what is on YouTube?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Not yet, Mr. President. We have staff members looking into the matter now. What I understood from the Defence at the break is -- I should say first, perhaps, we have received a version of these excerpts that does have audio, to answer Your Honour's first question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: But what I understood at the break is that the Defence is trying to locate their -- or is in the process of locating their downloaded full version of the video which is about 19 or 20 minutes long and is in the process of providing us with it, but we haven't received it yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did the Defence provide you at least with the exact cite location where they copied it from?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The surrogate sheet in e-court includes what we believe to be the address from which they downloaded. Though for completeness, it might be good -- I see Mr. Stojanovic nodding so I take it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- that that's confirmed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we'll leave it in your hands at this moment to further explore the details, background of this video. Let's have a look at the first excerpt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And let's now look at the second. Mr. Stojanovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, Your Honour, just a few questions about the first excerpt or should we move on to the second immediately?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, now, we do not hear anything now, not even the explosions, which is -- even if you do not rely on any text spoken, it might be relevant for the Chamber to listen at any explosions. As you may remember at an earlier video, the sound was, although not spoken text, pretty relevant. So could we look at it again but now with at least with the audio, although no need to translate, but just to be able to listen at any sound of explosions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Understood, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now we will look at and listen to the second excerpts. But if you first want to put questions to the witness, Mr. Stojanovic, you have an opportunity to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, just a few questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rasevic, do you recognise the footage?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise the footage and I recognise the feature shown.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is this the footage you indicated yesterday when we talked?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Which feature is this? In what area where the attack occurred?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: What we could see is part of Spicasta Stijena called Krs III. That was the most dominant feature. And what we will see in the next few moments is the attack on Krs I and Krs II, a few hundred metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would kindly ask that we see the next excerpt with the audio starting at 12 minutes, 20 seconds, to 13 minutes, 39 seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness first describe where he was when this happened and describe a bit more in detail what we see, if he has -- were you personally a witness of this event, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the time I was at the company command in the background of this feature some 200 metres away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you see from there what we see on this video?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not straight away. But when the first explosion occurred, I ran outside because I knew where the sound came from and then I did see it, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now the camera which is recording all this, is that behind your lines facing enemy positions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, the camera was placed on the other side, from Sedrenik, from the supermarket there. There was a hole and a mosque can be found there now. It was right next to the Sedrenik. That is where the market was, the shop, and they filmed it from there. It was done by a TV crew, the BH TV. Or so the people we can hear say when they are preparing for the attack.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, so this picture is taken to say from the -- from the city side, not from the Mrkovici side.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now the soldiers we see moving around a little bit left of where most of the explosion seems to -- seem to take place, what soldiers are they? Are they your soldiers or are they, as you called them, the so-called Army of the BiH soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They are the Black Swans soldiers belonging to the ABiH. They were the people who reached the outcrop and sneaked up behind our -- sneaked up to our positions and attacked them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, I saw some - and I'll repeat - I said I saw some explosions approximately at the level of where they were, just below the highest point. Do you -- did you also see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: All -- and those explosions were apparently from projectiles that were fired by whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The largest explosion we saw was caused by a hand-held rocket launcher. One could see them carrying it, the Black Swans, that is. There were several smaller explosions by hand-grenades, offensive, defensive type, et cetera, but the largest two or three were caused by the hand-held rocket launchers which are light to carry. All sabotage units have them when trying to take fortifications, for example.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But if you're talking about hand-grenades, who was throwing them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You could see that there were several of them there. And perhaps one or two of them had hand-held rocket launchers. The rest had infantry weapons --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and hand-grenades.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. You talked about hand-grenades exploding. Who had thrown those hand-grenades which exploded there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since they came up from their side, our soldiers threw hand-grenades from their trenches defending themselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we -- the explosions we see there are hand-grenades exploding amidst the -- as you call them, the Black Swans trying to climb up to the ridge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since our trench was hit by hand-held rocket launchers, our soldiers had a supply of hand-grenades. They were always there because it wasn't the first time the positions were attacked, and they responded, trying to see where the attackers were coming from. They threw hand-grenades to thwart their approach but the enemy continued and they had to withdraw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, again, you said you were - and let me just take you back to exactly what you said in this respect - you said you were at the company command at the background of this feature. Am I right in understanding that if we look at the picture we see that you are further back, so not the camera position, but rather 200 -- 200 metres further away from the camera position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I wasn't 200 metres away from the camera. I didn't see the camera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I said 200 metres further away from the camera. The camera shows us explosions, soldiers. Do I understand that you were 200 metres behind those soldiers and those explosions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Initial when the first detonation occurred and then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then you said you came out of your command post. You went outside. And you said then you could see everything. Could you see what happened because your command was behind the ridge, if I understand you well? Did you then approach the ridge to better be able to see it or ...?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, between my command post and the -- and the feature which was attacked, there was a backup or reserve command post which I approached immediately. We had reserve weapons there. One machine-gun was there. And then I could see everything unfolding as it was on the palm of my hand. And then I issued orders to withdraw to the backup trenches that we had dug there so that we could save the lives of our men.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let me stop you there for a second. So you withdrew from the front trenches to backup trenches a little bit further back. Now, from those front trenches, could you see what happened just below the ridge or couldn't you see it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We could not see that from those trenches, but they made a lot of noise, crying out, screaming, starting issuing threats, and bursts into the first trench that we saw. But stopped there, did not advance further, because they knew what was waiting for them there. And then from that side they tried to capture, as you will be able to see in the next video excerpt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. But what we therefore see on this video, that is, soldiers, exploding hand-grenades, which was just below the feature, you couldn't see that, if I understand you well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the moment when it was unfolding, I, of course, could not see. I saw my men throwing hand-grenades. Of course, this was beyond the ridge on the other side. There was a steep slope that I couldn't see from my viewpoint, them advancing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So what we see on the video you couldn't see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct. That's correct. I -- I could not see that with my own eyes. I only saw the smoke and the detonations and explosions up there. I could see my men withdrawing to the reserve trench, and I could see them occupying the outcrop or Krs III trench, the one that we saw on the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's move on and look. Yes, Judge Fluegge has one or more questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Just to understand the situation there. How often did you observe any fighting at the -- at that location, what we saw on the screen a minute ago?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean throughout my appointment as company commander there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, there were many attacks on that feature, on that section. I personally took part in fending them off. And on several occasions, that feature was not really captured but it would be abandoned by our men because they were afraid but -- and we would retake it no -- with no problems. But on that particular occasion it was tricky. It was really close.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, for the record. Let's take another excerpt from 20 seconds [as interpreted] to 13 minutes, 39 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rasevic, the feature that you can see in the centre of the screen, now this frozen frame, what was the name of that feature?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: That's Krs or outcrop III on Spicasta Stijena as they called it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Now please tell me: During this attack, did ABiH army members succeed in capturing that part of Spicasta Stijena?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me whether the VRS managed to recapture those positions at one point?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. As I just said, my army withdrew to a reserve or backup trench. There was one beyond this position. And there were two others to the right-hand side, two other trenches, which we held. And over night we secured them. We had brought in reinforcements until the morning. They spent the night in that particular trench. They started digging up to the trench. But we opened -- fired every 15, 20 minutes. We would toss a grenade in that direction to stop them from digging the trench further. And the next morning, the next day, we brought in our teams. They could not hold that position for long. There was no chance of them. That's first. Second, we could not let them capture those positions because this was the gateway.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I will ask you about this. Asked by His Honour Fluegge, you said that during your tenure as a company commander, this was one of the many attacks by the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: My question is: What was the reason why those attacks were so frequent to that -- on that particular position of VRS?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: My company, to our misfortune, occupied a strategically important position. And therefore, these are the dominant peaks. A ridge is a dominant feature. If they broke through this ridge, Spicasta Stijena, which was held by Mrkovici Company, they would have dominated that part of Sarajevo held by VRS units: Kosevo, Jagodina, Ilijas, Ilidza, Hadzici. Everything else would be encircled. Beyond this ridge, there is a road between Vogosca and Semizovac and Hresa and Romanija. That road is 250 metres from this ridge. So had this fallen, our families would have been in jeopardy. Our families, women, children, elderly, they would have to move away. And in terms of military advantage, had they captured this, they would have dominated all these localities that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: With respect to this feature, could you please place the Grdonj hill from this location?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: It was south to this. From this feature, our line then goes to the little fortress, or Mala Tvrdjava, and Grdonj hill is before this little fortress.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Grdonj hill, is it higher; that is, a greater elevation than the Spicasta Stijena?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is. If I'm not mistaken this is 895 and Grdonj is 906 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did ABiH members hold Grdonj throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, throughout the war. We could not -- we were never there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Rasevic. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would move -- mark for identification those two excerpts from the video which are 65 ter documents 1D02992. And once we've submitted the whole video to the Prosecution, then you will rule on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I don't have any objection to them being marked for identification only.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They will be marked for identification. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D2992 receives number D553, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D553 is marked for identification. I have a few more questions for you, Witness. You told us that at this occasion you recaptured the feature. Did it ever happen that the feature was for a longer period of time - that is, more than one or two days - under the control of the armed forces of BiH?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Never. Your Honours, it never occurred. The longest that they held to it was this time. They were there for 12 or 15 hours. They spent the night there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now you emphasised the strategic importance of the feature. Did you have sufficient sight over the parts of Sarajevo you mentioned from there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, well, we could see very well Sedrenik, Zlatiste, the barracks, or part of it, not the whole of it. Then Streliste, to the left-hand side, Grca Brdo and that would be it that we could see from that vantage point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So from the positions you were holding you could see, as you said, Sedrenik, Streliste, and I think you earlier mentioned Kosevo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we could see Kosevo from the Mala Tvrdjava, or small fortress. This is another position. This is opposite to this. We could not see Kosevo from this particular position, from this particular feature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But could you see Sedrenik from this particular position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it was not extremely dangerous to observe what happened down there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course it was dangerous. Well -- but soldiers had different means of protecting their positions, firing holes, bulwarks. Of course it was dangerous.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But you said you made such fortifications which allowed you still to look down and observe what happened below the feature. Is that how I have to understand your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, from those trenches and fortifications, we could not see what happened directly below us because these are vertical cliffs. They had their own shelters and dwelling places. But we could -- what we could see was a bit further afield. And up to 1993 we could monitor their lines because they were further away. But using cease-fires, they gained ground, and at one point we no longer could see all of their positions directly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now you talked about their lines up to 1993. Were their lines between the feature and Sedrenik or were their lines further afield behind Sedrenik seen from your position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, they were north of Sedrenik. Their lines were not at Sedrenik. Their lines stretched along the hill through Poglugov Dol in seven growths. There is a hill which we called Poglugov Brijeg, and the 887 hill, they held position. And then from Poglugov Brijeg, they opened sniping fire and two or three of our fighters were sniped at and wounded and hit from those positions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Earlier you said from those trenches and fortifications we could not see what happened directly below us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then later you say you could see -- what we could see was a bit further afield. And you said up to 1993 you could even monitor their lines, and their lines were closer -- were not in Sedrenik but closer to your positions. Does that mean that during all those times you would have a view, perhaps not always on their lines but at least on Sedrenik, from your shelters and your fortifications?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, their lines never were at Sedrenik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You told us that. But does that mean that since up to 1993 you could even see their lines that you always could have a look at Sedrenik from your fortification which was even further away than the lines of the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, yes. That was south -- further towards south from the lines of the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions in this respect. Mr. Traldi, are you ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I am, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Witness, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Traldi. You'll find him to your right. And Mr. Traldi is counsel for the Prosecution. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I want to start with a couple of brief questions about background events in March 1992. First, in paragraph 12 of your statement, you mentioned the death of Nikola Gardovic. And you say you heard about this at Mr. Gardovic's funeral; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. I do not understand the question. Could you please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you're looking at the screen, apparently. What are you looking at at this moment? Are you reading the English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This paragraph 12 appeared on the screen this very minute. I see the killing of Gardovic, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We have something different on our screen. There we are. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you heard about this event at his funeral; correct?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: You mean the event of the killing of Gardovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: No. I heard about this event in the media on TV on the very -- on the very night that he had been killed on Bascarsija.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: But you have no personal knowledge as how he died or who killed him, do you?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: No, except for what I saw from the media. At that time it was still a -- former Bosnia-Herzegovina or former Yugoslavia at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 10710.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As it comes up, sir, your evidence in your statement is that barricades were set up after this by the Serbian population and that it was spontaneous; is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, we see on page 1 that this is a letter from the Ministry of Internal Affairs, public security service, in Sarajevo. And it says we are forwarding you the list of employees of the SR BH MUP who took part in the activities related to the setting up of barracks in the region of Sarajevo in early March of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 5 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: At the top of the page in English and in the middle of the page in B/C/S, we read: "In Crisis Staff of SDS, among others, the following persons were engaged:" And the first two it mentions are Mandic, Momcilo, and Stanisic, Mico. Do you see those names, sir?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The Chamber has received evidence that both of these men would be senior officials in the Bosnian Serb police when it was created shortly thereafter, and that Mr. Mandic was a high official in the Bosnian MUP at this time. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I understood this correctly, this is erroneous that Mico Stanisic at that time was a high-level official of MUP of Bosnian Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're supposed not to give evidence, Mr. Stojanovic. You can test that evidence and bring to the attention of the witness. This is inappropriate to do. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If I could perhaps address my learned friend's concern. When I asked -- what I said was the Chamber has received evidence that these men would be senior officials in the Bosnian Serb police when it was created shortly after this, and that Mr. Mandic was a high official in the BH MUP at this time. And so I think the concern that Mr. Stojanovic raised does not arise from my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yeah, that's something different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So therefore two reasons why you should have remained seated: First, because you didn't carefully listen to the question. Second, your response was inappropriate. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, just to briefly summarise my question: Are you aware that Mr. Mandic and Mr. Stanisic would both become senior officials in the Bosnian police soon after this?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: I did not know that at the time because I did not deal with politics. It was foreign to me. Well, later on, when all these things happened, then I learned of those people. I could not specify who was minister, who was assistant minister though.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I put to you that what we see here indicates that Bosnian Serb officials and members of the SDS Crisis Staff were involved in setting up the barricades. I understand that what you've just said is you weren't aware of things like that at the time. Is that something you became aware of afterwards?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: No. I was never made aware of this. I hear of this for the first time from you. I really wasn't aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I see it may be time for the break. Before we take it, I'd tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 10710 seize number P6634, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6634 is admitted. Witness, we'll take a break and we'd like to see you back in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll resume at 10 minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we are waiting for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom, I didn't hear any negative responses by the parties on the suggested change in the times a few days late September/early October; that is, to start at 9.00 so as to ensure that we still would have morning sessions when other cases need additional time. Therefore, the Chamber will confirm through the Registry that we agree for those few days in sitting starting at 9.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that would be Courtroom III. Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, you were a member of the Serbian Democratic Party when it was established in 1990; correct?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 30878. This is a confirmation -- or this will be a confirmation signed by Radovan Karadzic and dated the 21st of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, looking at the list of names on the document, you recognise all five of those names; correct?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: I see four names and I know all four.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you see your own name at number 4?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And this document is a list of members being appointed to the war commission of the Serbian municipality of Sarajevo centre; correct?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I'd tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30878 receives number P6635, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And just one more brief area regarding political matters, sir. Once the conflict began, you heard that one of the goals of the Bosnian Serb leadership was to divide Sarajevo; correct?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: At first that was not the goal of Bosnian Serbs. First of all, we were not in favour of a war and we were all thrown into it. I went to Mrkovici on the 4th of April, 1992. I was out of the information loop because problems were so great and I had no time to deal with anything other than to save my men.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I stop you there, Witness. First of all, the question is, if you would have carefully listened to it, said, "Once the conflict began," so there is no reason to further explore whether you wanted that or not, but once the conflict began did you hear that one of the goals of the Bosnian Serb leadership was to divide Sarajevo. Did you hear that or did you not hear that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I didn't hear about that at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. Did you hear it at any later stage, then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Later on there was some mention of it during the war. When people realised that we could no longer live together, then the idea of splitting Sarajevo up in two came up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If Mr. Traldi wants an explanation, he'll ask for it. So the answer is you later learned about it. Mr. Traldi, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And to follow up --

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: To follow up on your answer, sir, you said: "People realised that we could no longer live together." Did you also learn that one of the goals of the leadership was separate Muslim and Serb territories?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: It appeared later. It wasn't one of the goals at first. Later on it became a goal and the territory was split.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You say it wasn't one of the goals at first. A moment ago you said you were out of the information loop at first. So would I be correct that what you mean to say is you heard about it later on?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: Well, much later, when it fell through -- well, we thought that there were combat incidents and we took up territory awaiting a political settlement. We didn't know what it would turn out to be as soldiers. We were in the trenches. Only later this realisation came about that no agreement would be possible, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I want to turn then to your military career very briefly. You first war platoon commander; correct?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You became a platoon commander before the VRS was created; right?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: At that time when you first became a platoon commander, what was the name of the company in which you were a platoon commander?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: We founded the company. It consisted of the villagers, volunteers who reported. It was called the Mrkovici Company or the company of Mrkovici, and that name stayed with us throughout the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: At that time was your company part -- and I'm speaking of April 1992, was your company part of a larger armed formation?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We were attached to the Hresa Battalion which had been established at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the first commander of your company was Bojo Dragec; right?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: The first commander of our unit was Veseljko Dragec. Bojo -- actually, I commanded the first platoon and Bojo commanded the second platoon. Then we were joined by a group of people from Barice to the left of us and we used them to establish the third platoon commanded by Milovan --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness kindly repeat the last name. We did not hear it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I think you've been asked to repeat the name of the commander of the third platoon.

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: The commander of the third platoon was Milovan Baricanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, when the VRS was formed you became a platoon commander in the Hresa Battalion of the 2nd Romanija Motorised Brigade of the VRS; correct?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Immediately upon establishment of the VRS, we fell under the command of the 2nd Romanija Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You said your company was called the Mrkovici Company. The companies in the 2nd Romanija Brigade had not just names but numbers; correct? 1st Company, 2nd Company, 3rd Company?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: What is the number of your company?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: At the beginning when we were made part of the Romanija Light Brigade, we were the 3rd Company of the -- what I think at the time was the 5th Battalion, the Hresa Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And when you were platoon commander, did you also become deputy commander of the company?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Automatically per establishment the 1st Platoon commander was also deputy company commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you later in January 1993 became company commander; right?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As a platoon commander and a company commander, it was your responsibility to know what SRK units in the vicinity of your area of responsibility were doing; right?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was my responsibility to know, of course. I was responsible for the area of responsibility of my company and those immediately ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think the end of your answer may not have been translated. You said you were also responsible for the companies immediately adjoining your company?

utterances.speaker: BLASKO RASEVIC
utterances.text: No. I was responsible for my company. And of course I was interested in what the formations to my left and right were and how they worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You mention in your statement that your battalion, that's the Hresa Battalion, was transferred to the 1st Romanija Brigade. That was around the beginning of September 1992; correct?
